newsitem.title: MEXICO: La Moderna second quarter results disappoint.
newsitem.headline: La Moderna second quarter results disappoint.

text.p: Mexico's cigarette and agro-biotechnology giant Empresas La Moderna SA de CV's second quarter results were clearly disappointing, coming in below expectations, analysts said on Tuesday.
"They were pretty bad," said Smith Barney analyst Francisco Chavez.
Second quarter total sales were 3.498 billion pesos, eight percent less than the 3.815 bilion pesos reported in the same period a year earlier.
There was weakness in all three of the company's divisions.
Operating profit in the agro-biotechnology division fell 44 percent in the second quarter versus the year-ago quarter to 230 million pesos.
The cigarette division's operating profits were 217 million pesos compared with 335 million pesos in the second quarter a year earlier.
Packaging division operating profits were 105 million pesos, down 49 percent from the same period a year earlier.
La Moderna's overall operating profits were 320 million pesos in the second quarter.
"There were mitigating circumstances with the report, though. They had a plant shutdown that very negatively affected the results of (the packaging) division," Chavez said.
That forced the packaging divison to buy products just to satisfy customers.
Cigarette prices and volumes were down due to smuggling, analysts said, while agro-biotechnology, including the food division, was weak on poor harvests and other reasons.
"All three divisions had problems," Chavez said.
A survey of three analysts by Reuters done before the results were released found expectations of revenues of 4.38 billion pesos and operating income of 609 million pesos.
Merrill Lynch analyst Alyce Andrews had had a forecast of 3.5 billion pesos in revenues and 442 million pesos in operating profit for the quarter.
"Obviously it (operating profit) was below my estimates so it was disappointing, but one of the biggest shortfalls is the cigarette division, which they are effectively divesting," said Andrews.
Earlier in the month, La Moderna announced that it had sold half of its cigarette business to Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc in order to focus more on its agrobiotechnology side.
Under the deal, B.A.T is to boost Cigarrera La Moderna's share capital by $1.712 billion in a complicated deal.
Analysts say one unknown is what the company plans to do with all its cash.
Moderna's share price weakened on Wednesday, trading down 70 centavos to 42.90 pesos in mid-day trade.
((--Mexico City newsroom +525 728 9559))
